content: 1. Erythromycin stearate is contraindicated in cases of QTc interval prolongation. Avoid coadministration with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. If such drugs must be used, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 2. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is coadministered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 3. Erythromycin stearate and vandetanib both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of vemurafenib by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with drugs that prolong the QT interval is not recommended. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50%. Monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 6. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and verapamil increases erythromycin stearate levels through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise caution when vilanterol is coadministered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur, reduce the daily dose of vilazodone to 20 mg. 9. Voriconazole increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Erythromycin stearate and vorinostat both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Zafirlukast increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of zavegepant intranasal by mechanisms involving OATP1B3 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant. 13. Erythromycin stearate and ziprasidone both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Decrease the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 15. Erythromycin stearate and albuterol both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of aliskiren by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of amifampridine, which can cause seizures. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. 22. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of amikacin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Erythromycin stearate and apomorphine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Erythromycin stearate and arformoterol both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Erythromycin stearate and aripiprazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and OATP1B1 inhibition. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The recommended dosage of atogepant with OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. 30. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of atorvastatin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and associated adverse events. 32. Azithromycin and erythromycin stearate both increase the QTc interval. Azithromycin increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin stearate and bedaquiline both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 37. Belzutifan decreases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. If coadministration cannot be avoided, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 38. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of bendamustine by reducing its metabolism to active metabolites. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 41. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of bromocriptine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of budesonide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Monitor for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary. 49. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Monitor plasma levels to ensure adequacy. Transition back to a formulation that permits dose adjustments if toxicity occurs. 50. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose. 54. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the capivasertib dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 55. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of cefdinir by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 56. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of cefditoren by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of cefoxitin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of cefpodoxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of ceftriaxone by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of cefuroxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Cenobamate decreases the levels of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed. 62. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Ciprofloxacin and erythromycin stearate both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration may increase the risk of torsades de pointes in predisposed patients. 66. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 67. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. 70. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of cortisone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crizotinib also increases erythromycin stearate levels through the same mechanism.
